{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_fd98043d16634a9e865831e1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Existing tools for browsing/monitoring the Hetzner Server Auction\n2\t\n3\tSurvey of third-party tools, dashboards, bots, and libraries that already do some\n4\tversion of \"browse/filter/monitor Hetzner's dedicated server auction,\" done before\n5\tbuilding this project's feature set. All entries were checked live in August 2026\n6\t(web search + page/README fetch + GitHub API for stars/last-push where applicable).\n7\tThis market moves fast and repos disappear/rename often — treat \"active\" status as\n8\ta snapshot, not a guarantee.\n9\t\n10\t---\n11\t\n12\t## 1. Server Radar (a.k.a. \"hetzner-radar\")\n13\t\n14\t- **URL(s):** https://radar.iodev.org/ (also mirrored at https://server-radar.pages.dev/)\n15\t- **Repo:** https://github.com/elsbrock/hetzner-radar\n16\t- **Status:** **Very active.** 366 stars, 16 forks, 919 commits, last push same day as\n17\t  this research (2026-08-01). By far the most popular and polished tool found in this\n18\t  survey.\n19\t- **Architecture note:** SvelteKit frontend + **DuckDB-WASM for client-side\n20\t  filtering**, with a Cloudflare Workers / GitHub Actions pipeline feeding Cloudflare\n21\t  D1 and R2. This is architecturally the closest sibling to the plan for this\n22\t  project (static frontend, DuckDB-WASM, no client-side joins) — see\n23\t  `docs/plan/plan.md` and `docs/notes/benchmark-priority.md`.\n24\t- **Features confirmed:**\n25\t  - Filter by CPU (model/core count), RAM, storage type/size, location/datacenter\n26\t  - Advertises itself as comparing auction prices against Hetzner's standard\n27\t    dedicated and cloud SKUs in one filterable view\n28\t  - **Price history:** ~3 months retained per configuration; shows lowest price ever\n29\t    seen for a given config, daily price index vs. a rolling baseline, min €/GB RAM,\n30\t    min €/TB storage, AMD vs. Intel and ECC vs. non-ECC spreads, listing volume by\n31\t    country/datacenter/CPU (see `/statistics` and `/guide` pages)\n32\t  - **Alerts:** target-price alerts via email and Discord webhook (with fallback\n33\t    logic), plus cloud-availability-by-location alerts\n34\t  - **Refresh:** auction data polled every 5 minutes via two parallel pipelines;\n35\t    cloud availability checked every 60 seconds; client-side DuckDB purges records\n36\t    older than 90 days\n37\t  - Free, open source, no login required to browse (accounts only needed for alerts)\n38\t- **Features NOT found:** no CPU benchmark scores (PassMark/Geekbench/anything) of\n39\t  any kind, no documented public API, no comparison/side-by-side view, no\n40\t  auto-buy/sniping. A LowEndTalk thread about this tool (202410) has no mention of\n41\t  benchmarking as a request or gap — discussion is purely positive/UI-focused.\n42\t- **Bottom line:** the category leader on breadth, history, and alerting — and a\n43\t  clean confirmation that **the most mature, most-used tool in this space has zero\n44\t  CPU-benchmark integration.**\n45\t\n46\t## 2. Hetzner Auction Browser+ (a.k.a. \"Hetzner Value Auctions\")\n47\t\n48\t- **URL(s):** https://auction.akua.dev/ (about page: `/about`); also republished at\n49\t  https://hetzner-value-auctions.cnap.tech/guide (`cnap.tech/blog/...` redirects to\n50\t  `akua.dev/blog/...`, same author)\n51\t- **Status:** Appears to be a single-developer side project; blog post (2026-04-29)\n52\t  cites ~36,400 page views and ~6,490 unique visitors \"since January [2026],\" so it\n53\t  has real usage but is much smaller than Server Radar. No GitHub repo was surfaced\n54\t  (may be closed-source or unlisted).\n55\t- **Features confirmed:**\n56\t  - **This is the clearest CPU-benchmark implementation found.** Live auction data\n57\t    is \"enriched with PassMark CPU benchmark scores.\" Two explicit value metrics:\n58\t    **CPUMark/€** (raw processing power per euro) and a blended **Total Score**.\n59\t  - Total Score methodology (from the `/about` page): CPU performance via PassMark\n60\t    \"enhanced with our own scaling algorithm,\" RAM scored with a 20% bonus for ECC,\n61\t    storage weighted NVMe=2x / SSD=1x / HDD=0.5x, plus network bandwidth and CPU TDP\n62\t    (efficiency) factored in\n63\t  - Filter by CPU performance range, RAM, price (with ~5% tolerance band), location\n64\t    (by country/region), and boolean requirements: IPv6, NVMe, ECC\n65\t  - Sort by price range and CPU-score-per-euro\n66\t  - Mentions a **server comparison view** (side-by-side), mobile-responsive, dark\n67\t    mode\n68\t  - Real-time pull from Hetzner's live auction API\n69\t- **Features NOT found:** no price history/trend tracking, no alerts/saved\n70\t  searches, no documented API, no auto-buy.\n71\t- **Bottom line:** the best precedent for \"PassMark score joined onto live\n72\t  listings + blended value score,\" but it's a much smaller/less-maintained project\n73\t  than Server Radar, has no history, and (like everything else found) sources from\n74\t  PassMark only — never Geekbench.\n75\t\n76\t## 3. hzfind\n77\t\n78\t- **URL:** https://github.com/clouedoc/hzfind\n79\t- **Status:** Active-ish. 81 stars, 3 forks, last push 2026-05-23. Rust, MIT\n80\t  licensed, requires Rust 2024 edition.\n81\t- **Type:** CLI/TUI, not a web dashboard.\n82\t- **Features confirmed:**\n83\t  - Fetches live Hetzner auction data\n84\t  - **PassMark CPU benchmarks bundled directly in the binary** (no external API\n85\t    call needed to score a listing)\n86\t  - Filters: max monthly price (`p`), minimum CPU score (`s`), minimum core count\n87\t    (`c`)\n88\t  - Sort by CPU value (score/€), storage value (GB/€), RAM value (GB/€) — i.e. three\n89\t    separate price-per-metric rankings, not one blended score\n90\t  - Optional comparison against a Hetzner Cloud CCX33 baseline (€62.99/mo) to show\n91\t    when auction hardware beats renting cloud\n92\t- **Features NOT found:** no price history, no alerts, no comparison view beyond\n93\t  the single cloud baseline, no API, no location/network/disk-type filters\n94\t  documented, no auto-buy.\n95\t- **Bottom line:** second confirmed PassMark implementation, terminal-only, smaller\n96\t  in scope than Auction Browser+ (no blended score, no RAM/disk-type filtering\n97\t  documented) but notable for being genuinely CPU-score-first in its UX — sorting by\n98\t  value-per-euro is the primary interaction, not an add-on.\n99\t\n100\t## 4. Server Auction Tracker (madfam-org)\n101\t\n102\t- **Repo:** https://github.com/madfam-org/server-auction-tracker\n103\t- **Live site:** https://sniper.madfam.io (confirmed reachable — HTTP 200 via curl;\n104\t  WebFetch's own fetcher got a 403, likely bot/Cloudflare protection, so UI content\n105\t  couldn't be independently verified beyond the README's claims)\n106\t- **Status:** Small/early. **0 stars, 0 forks**, 69 commits, last push 2026-06-14.\n107\t  Treat feature claims below with more caution than the above tools since GitHub\n108\t  traction is essentially nil and the live UI wasn't independently rendered.\n109\t- **Features claimed (from README/docs):**\n110\t  - Filters: RAM, CPU cores, drives, price, datacenter, ECC, NVMe; **shareable\n111\t    filter URLs** for bookmarking\n112\t  - **Third confirmed PassMark integration**, covering \"~90 processor models,\"\n113\t    normalized against the highest-performing server in each scan; weighted scoring\n114\t    (CPU 0.25, RAM 0.20, storage 0.15, + other factors) scaled to a 0–100 score with\n115\t    \"deal quality\" labels\n116\t  - Price history via SQLite: min/max/avg stats per CPU model, deal-quality\n117\t    calculations\n118\t  - Dashboard charts: AMD vs. Intel price trends, datacenter distribution, top\n119\t    value CPUs\n120\t  - Alerts: Slack, Discord, Webhook, Telegram, min-score thresholds, curated\n121\t    daily/weekly digest\n122\t  - **Cluster simulation** (testing whether a set of servers meets a capacity\n123\t    target) — a genuinely unique feature not seen elsewhere\n124\t  - **Claimed auto-ordering**: Hetzner Robot API integration for automatic purchase\n125\t    with configurable safety gates and a \"Buy Now\" two-step confirmation flow, plus\n126\t    order audit logs\n127\t  - CLI tool (`foundry-scout`) in addition to the web dashboard (`deal-sniper`)\n128\t- **Bottom line:** on paper the single most feature-complete tool found — PassMark\n129\t  scoring, history, alerts, AND auto-buy — but the near-zero GitHub traction and\n130\t  inability to verify the live UI means this should be read as \"most ambitious\n131\t  README,\" not confirmed best-in-class. If real, it's the only tool combining\n132\t  benchmark scoring with actual purchase automation.\n133\t\n134\t## 5. Hetzner Server Auction Monitor (Apify actor)\n135\t\n136\t- **URL:** https://apify.com/rl1987/hetzner-server-auction-monitor\n137\t- **Status:** Active, commercially hosted on Apify's platform (pay-per-use).\n138\t- **Features confirmed:**\n139\t  - Filters: max price (EUR/USD), min RAM, ECC-only toggle, disk type\n140\t    (NVMe/SATA/HDD) + min capacity, datacenter prefix (FSN/NBG/HEL/etc.),\n141\t    case-insensitive CPU model match\n142\t  - Alerts via generic JSON webhook or native Apify integrations; de-duplicates so\n143\t    each server triggers only one notification across polls\n144\t  - Configurable schedule, default every 10 minutes, cron-customizable\n145\t  - **Genuine API access** (it's an Apify Actor — JS/Python/REST/CLI clients all\n146\t    work) at $1 per 1,000 checks (~$1.44–$4.32/month at typical polling rates)\n147\t- **Features NOT found:** no sorting, no price-per-metric, no CPU benchmarks, no\n148\t  price history, no comparison view.\n149\t- **Bottom line:** a pure filter+webhook monitor sold as infrastructure, not a\n150\t  dashboard. Useful data point that \"API access\" as a feature exists in this space,\n151\t  just not bundled with any analysis features.\n152\t\n153\t## 6. hetzner-auction-discord-bot (Quintenvw)\n154\t\n155\t- **URL:** https://github.com/Quintenvw/hetzner-auction-discord-bot\n156\t- **Status:** Active. 37 stars, 4 forks, last push 2026-04-27.\n157\t- **Type:** Discord bot, MongoDB-backed per-user filter configs.\n158\t- **Features confirmed:** filter by CPU type, RAM (capacity + ECC), storage\n159\t  (HDD size/quantity/type), location, price threshold with VAT calc, currency\n160\t  (EUR/USD); posts direct links and @-mentions matching users; stale configs\n161\t  auto-expire after 90 days of no matches.\n162\t- **Features NOT found:** no sorting, no price-per-metric, no CPU benchmarks, no\n163\t  history, no comparison, no API, no auto-buy.\n164\t- **Bottom line:** solid, actively-used notification bot; pure filter-and-ping, no\n165\t  analysis layer.\n166\t\n167\t## 7. hetzner-notify (RickBakkr)\n168\t\n169\t- **URL:** https://github.com/RickBakkr/hetzner-notify\n170\t- **Status:** **Dead.** 27 stars, 6 forks, last push 2018-10-06 (~8 years stale).\n171\t  Included for completeness / to show how much churn this niche has — most tools\n172\t  from the 2018-era Hetzner \"Serverbörse\" webhook-bot wave are abandoned.\n173\t- **Features:** webhook-based notifications of new auction listings. No benchmark,\n174\t  history, or filtering sophistication documented beyond basic matching.\n175\t\n176\t## 8. hetzner-auction-hunter (danielskowronski)\n177\t\n178\t- **URL:** https://github.com/danielskowronski/hetzner-auction-hunter\n179\t- **Status:** Semi-stale. 108 stars, 23 forks (highest star count of the\n180\t  notification-bot category), but last push 2024-08-09 — no activity in ~2 years.\n181\t- **Type:** CLI/cron notification tool, very broad notification-channel support\n182\t  (Pushover, SimplePush, Slack, Gmail, SMTP, Telegram, Gitter, Pushbullet, Join,\n183\t  Zulip, Twilio, PagerDuty, Mailgun, PopcornNotify, StatusPage.io, iCloud,\n184\t  VictorOps) via the `notifiers` library.\n185\t- **Features confirmed:** filter by max price, disk count/capacity/min-per-disk\n186\t  size, SSD/NVMe requirement, CPU count, RAM, ECC, hardware RAID, redundant PSU,\n187\t  discrete GPU, IPv4 availability, Intel NIC, datacenter/region; configurable VAT\n188\t  (defaults 19% DE); dedup via local state file; JSON payload passthrough; dry-run\n189\t  test mode.\n190\t- **Features NOT found:** no CPU benchmarks, no price history, no comparison view,\n191\t  no documented API, no auto-buy. Refresh depends entirely on user's own cron\n192\t  setup.\n193\t- **Bottom line:** the most exhaustive raw hardware-filter list of any tool\n194\t  surveyed (RAID, PSU, GPU, NIC vendor) — a good reference for \"what filter fields\n195\t  power users actually want\" even though it's stale and has zero\n196\t  performance-normalization.\n197\t\n198\t## 9. hetzner-auction (robpickerill)\n199\t\n200\t- **URL:** https://github.com/robpickerill/hetzner-auction\n201\t- **Status:** **Dead / minimal.** 1 star, 0 forks, 16 commits, last push\n202\t  2020-11-01.\n203\t- **Features:** posts servers of interest to Slack on a daily Lambda schedule.\n204\t  No filters, sorting, benchmarks, history, or API documented — essentially a\n205\t  personal utility script.\n206\t\n207\t## 10. hetzner-cli (ytspar)\n208\t\n209\t- **URL:** https://github.com/ytspar/hetzner-cli\n210\t- **Status:** Active. 0 stars/forks but last push 2026-07-15 (very recent);\n211\t  positioned as a \"feature-complete\" general Robot API CLI/Node library, not\n212\t  auction-specific.\n213\t- **Features confirmed (auction subcommands):**\n214\t  - Rich filters: price (min/max monthly, hourly cap, setup fee), fixed-price vs.\n215\t    true-auction distinction, CPU model match, socket/core counts, RAM + ECC,\n216\t    total disk capacity range, drive count, drive type (NVMe/SATA/HDD), datacenter,\n217\t    bandwidth minimum, GPU presence, Intel NIC, high-I/O flag\n218\t  - **Sorting** across the widest field list found in this survey: price, hourly,\n219\t    setup, ram, disk, disk_count, cpu, cpu_count, datacenter, bandwidth,\n220\t    next_reduce (asc/desc), plus `--limit`\n221\t  - `--json` output for scripting/`jq` piping; a `--direct` flag to bypass its own\n222\t    15-minute hosted cache; `auction status`, `auction diff` (snapshot comparison),\n223\t    and `auction watch` (poll for changes) subcommands; offline fallback cache with\n224\t    stale-data warnings on stderr\n225\t  - Exports filtering/sorting/fetch functions as a library for Node automation\n226\t- **Features NOT found:** no CPU benchmark scoring, no price history persistence\n227\t  beyond diff/watch, no alerts/notification delivery, no comparison view, no\n228\t  auto-buy.\n229\t- **Bottom line:** the most complete raw filter+sort+fetch primitive of anything\n230\t  surveyed, and a good sanity check on \"what sort dimensions are table stakes\" —\n231\t  but it's explicitly a low-level API client, not a decision-support tool, and has\n232\t  no performance normalization at all.\n233\t\n234\t## 11. Get Hetzner (gethetzner.com)\n235\t\n236\t- **URL:** https://gethetzner.com/products/auction/\n237\t- **Status:** Live commercial site.\n238\t- **Type:** Not a monitoring tool — a **reseller/marketplace front-end** for\n239\t  Hetzner-class hardware (EX/AX/SX/GPU/Dell lines), claiming 5-minute inventory\n240\t  refresh and offering filters for CPU type, RAM, storage/disk config. No CPU\n241\t  benchmark data. Included because it surfaced repeatedly in searches and could be\n242\t  mistaken for an auction dashboard; it's adjacent, not a direct comparator.\n243\t\n244\t---\n245\t\n246\t## Adjacent but out-of-scope (context, not direct competitors)\n247\t\n248\t- **achromatic.dev — \"Hetzner Server Comparison 2026\" (blog post):** a *static*\n249\t  article, not a live tool, that does join PassMark (dedicated) and a cloud-VPS\n250\t  benchmark score to Hetzner's **standard catalog** pricing — but it **explicitly\n251\t  excludes the Server Auction** (\"this comparison intentionally excludes servers\n252\t  listed on Hetzner's Server Auction platform, which employs a descending-price\n253\t  Dutch auction mechanism\"). This is a useful signal: even a\n254\t  benchmark-comparison-focused writer treated the auction's constantly-rotating,\n255\t  heterogeneous CPU inventory as too much of a moving target for a static join —\n256\t  which is exactly the kind of pipeline work this project is committing to\n257\t  automate.\n258\t- **ServerHunter (serverhunter.com)** and **serverlist.dev:** multi-provider\n259\t  (79,000+ servers across ~930 hosting companies) price/availability comparison\n260\t  engines. Long-running (ServerHunter since 2013/2018), 24-hour refresh, stock\n261\t  alerts every 15 minutes. Not Hetzner-auction-specific and no evidence of CPU\n262\t  benchmark integration — they compare list-price hosting plans generally, not\n263\t  the Dutch-auction mechanic specifically.\n264\t- **Geekbench Browser (browser.geekbench.com) / VPSBenchmarks / BareMetalBench:**\n265\t  these are where actual Geekbench/YABS benchmark *runs* for specific\n266\t  Hetzner-auction-purchased machines end up — individual buyers post results after\n267\t  the fact (e.g. \"Hetzner Server Auction i5-12500,\" \"Hetzner - Auction Server Yab\n268\t  October 2024\"). This is real Geekbench data that exists in the wild tied to\n269\t  Hetzner auction hardware, but it is **disconnected, manual, and after-the-fact**:\n270\t  nobody has joined this data back onto the *live* auction feed for filtering or\n271\t  sorting. It's a corpus that a future benchmark-matching pipeline could\n272\t  potentially mine, not a competing product.\n273\t- **API client libraries** (`hrobot-rs`, `aszlig/hetzner`, `Radiergummi/hetzner-api-client`,\n274\t  `nl2go/hetzner-robot-api-mock`): general-purpose Hetzner Robot API clients in\n275\t  Rust/Python/Node used to *build* tools like the above. Not end-user products\n276\t  themselves; noted only because they surfaced heavily in searches for\n277\t  \"Hetzner auction JSON parser.\"\n278\t- **Official Hetzner Server Auction FAQ** (docs.hetzner.com): confirms the native\n279\t  UI supports basic filtering (price, RAM, drive count, free-text like \"Epyc\" /\n280\t  \"Xeon\" / \"DDR4\") but documents no sorting beyond that, no API, no refresh-rate\n281\t  disclosure, and no performance/benchmark data of any kind — the floor every\n282\t  third-party tool is improving on.\n283\t\n284\t---\n285\t\n286\t## Feature landscape: table-stakes vs. differentiating vs. gaps\n287\t\n288\t### Table stakes (present in nearly every tool surveyed)\n289\t- Filter by **price**, **RAM**, **disk type/size**, **CPU model or core count**,\n290\t  and **location/datacenter** — every single tool above implements this core set.\n291\t- Some form of **alerting/notification** (email, Discord, Slack, Telegram,\n292\t  webhook, Pushover, etc.) is present in 7 of the 11 direct tools — it's more\n293\t  common than not, especially among the bot-style tools.\n294\t- Polling cadence in the **5–15 minute** range is the norm across every tool that\n295\t  documents it (Server Radar: 5 min; gethetzner.com: 5 min; Apify actor default:\n296\t  10 min; hetzner-cli hosted cache: 15 min) — this roughly tracks how often\n297\t  Hetzner's own Dutch-auction prices step down.\n298\t- ECC and NVMe/SSD/HDD as explicit boolean/enum filters are near-universal once a\n299\t  tool has any disk/RAM filtering at all.\n300\t\n301\t### Common, but not universal\n302\t- **Price-per-metric** (€/GB RAM, €/TB storage) — present as an aggregate stat in\n303\t  Server Radar's `/statistics` page, and as a per-listing sort key in hzfind\n304\t  (GB/€ for RAM and storage), but most of the notification-bot-style tools skip it\n305\t  entirely.\n306\t- **Price history / trend tracking** — Server Radar (3 months) and\n307\t  Server Auction Tracker (SQLite, claimed) have it; All entries were checked live in August 2026\n(web search + page/README fetch + GitHub API for stars/last-push where applicable).\nThis market moves fast and repos disappear/rename often — treat \"active\" status as\na snapshot, not a guarantee.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Server Radar (a.k.a. \"hetzner-radar\")\n\n- **URL(s):** https://radar.iodev.org/ (also mirrored at https://server-radar.pages.dev/)\n- **Repo:** https://github.com/elsbrock/hetzner-radar\n- **Status:** **Very active.** 366 stars, 16 forks, 919 commits, last push same day as\n  this research (2026-08-01). By far the most popular and polished tool found in this\n  survey.\n- **Architecture note:** SvelteKit frontend + **DuckDB-WASM for client-side\n  filtering**, with a Cloudflare Workers / GitHub Actions pipeline feeding Cloudflare\n  D1 and R2. This is architecturally the closest sibling to the plan for this\n  project (static frontend, DuckDB-WASM, no client-side joins) — see\n  `docs/plan/plan.md` and `docs/notes/benchmark-priority.md`.\n- **Features confirmed:**\n  - Filter by CPU (model/core count), RAM, storage type/size, location/datacenter\n  - Advertises itself as comparing auction prices against Hetzner's standard\n    dedicated and cloud SKUs in one filterable view\n  - **Price history:** ~3 months retained per configuration; shows lowest price ever\n    seen for a given config, daily price index vs. a rolling baseline, min €/GB RAM,\n    min €/TB storage, AMD vs. Intel and ECC vs. non-ECC spreads, listing volume by\n    country/datacenter/CPU (see `/statistics` and `/guide` pages)\n  - **Alerts:** target-price alerts via email and Discord webhook (with fallback\n    logic), plus cloud-availability-by-location alerts\n  - **Refresh:** auction data polled every 5 minutes via two parallel pipelines;\n    cloud availability checked every 60 seconds; client-side DuckDB purges records\n    older than 90 days\n  - Free, open source, no login required to browse (accounts only needed for alerts)\n- **Features NOT found:** no CPU benchmark scores (PassMark/Geekbench/anything) of\n  any kind, no documented public API, no comparison/side-by-side view, no\n  auto-buy/sniping. A LowEndTalk thread about this tool (202410) has no mention of\n  benchmarking as a request or gap — discussion is purely positive/UI-focused.\n- **Bottom line:** the category leader on breadth, history, and alerting — and a\n  clean confirmation that **the most mature, most-used tool in this space has zero\n  CPU-benchmark integration.**\n\n## 2. Hetzner Auction Browser+ (a.k.a. \"Hetzner Value Auctions\")\n\n- **URL(s):** https://auction.akua.dev/ (about page: `/about`); also republished at\n  https://hetzner-value-auctions.cnap.tech/guide (`cnap.tech/blog/...` redirects to\n  `akua.dev/blog/...`, same author)\n- **Status:** Appears to be a single-developer side project; blog post (2026-04-29)\n  cites ~36,400 page views and ~6,490 unique visitors \"since January [2026],\" so it\n  has real usage but is much smaller than Server Radar. No GitHub repo was surfaced\n  (may be closed-source or unlisted).\n- **Features confirmed:**\n  - **This is the clearest CPU-benchmark implementation found.** Live auction data\n    is \"enriched with PassMark CPU benchmark scores.\" Two explicit value metrics:\n    **CPUMark/€** (raw processing power per euro) and a blended **Total Score**.\n  - Total Score methodology (from the `/about` page): CPU performance via PassMark\n    \"enhanced with our own scaling algorithm,\" RAM scored with a 20% bonus for ECC,\n    storage weighted NVMe=2x / SSD=1x / HDD=0.5x, plus network bandwidth and CPU TDP\n    (efficiency) factored in\n  - Filter by CPU performance range, RAM, price (with ~5% tolerance band), location\n    (by country/region), and boolean requirements: IPv6, NVMe, ECC\n  - Sort by price range and CPU-score-per-euro\n  - Mentions a **server comparison view** (side-by-side), mobile-responsive, dark\n    mode\n  - Real-time pull from Hetzner's live auction API\n- **Features NOT found:** no price history/trend tracking, no alerts/saved\n  searches, no documented API, no auto-buy.\n- **Bottom line:** the best precedent for \"PassMark score joined onto live\n  listings + blended value score,\" but it's a much smaller/less-maintained project\n  than Server Radar, has no history, and (like everything else found) sources from\n  PassMark only — never Geekbench.\n\n## 3. hzfind\n\n- **URL:** https://github.com/clouedoc/hzfind\n- **Status:** Active-ish. 81 stars, 3 forks, last push 2026-05-23. Rust, MIT\n  licensed, requires Rust 2024 edition.\n- **Type:** CLI/TUI, not a web dashboard.\n- **Features confirmed:**\n  - Fetches live Hetzner auction data\n  - **PassMark CPU benchmarks bundled directly in the binary** (no external API\n    call needed to score a listing)\n  - Filters: max monthly price (`p`), minimum CPU score (`s`), minimum core count\n    (`c`)\n  - Sort by CPU value (score/€), storage value (GB/€), RAM value (GB/€) — i.e. three\n    separate price-per-metric rankings, not one blended score\n  - Optional comparison against a Hetzner Cloud CCX33 baseline (€62.99/mo) to show\n    when auction hardware beats renting cloud\n- **Features NOT found:** no price history, no alerts, no comparison view beyond\n  the single cloud baseline, no API, no location/network/disk-type filters\n  documented, no auto-buy.\n- **Bottom line:** second confirmed PassMark implementation, terminal-only, smaller\n  in scope than Auction Browser+ (no blended score, no RAM/disk-type filtering\n  documented) but notable for being genuinely CPU-score-first in its UX — sorting by\n  value-per-euro is the primary interaction, not an add-on.\n\n## 4. If real, it's the only tool combining\n  benchmark scoring with actual purchase automation.\n\n## 5. Hetzner Server Auction Monitor (Apify actor)\n\n- **URL:** https://apify.com/rl1987/hetzner-server-auction-monitor\n- **Status:** Active, commercially hosted on Apify's platform (pay-per-use).\n- **Features confirmed:**\n  - Filters: max price (EUR/USD), min RAM, ECC-only toggle, disk type\n    (NVMe/SATA/HDD) + min capacity, datacenter prefix (FSN/NBG/HEL/etc.),\n    case-insensitive CPU model match\n  - Alerts via generic JSON webhook or native Apify integrations; de-duplicates so\n    each server triggers only one notification across polls\n  - Configurable schedule, default every 10 minutes, cron-customizable\n  - **Genuine API access** (it's an Apify Actor — JS/Python/REST/CLI clients all\n    work) at $1 per 1,000 checks (~$1.44–$4.32/month at typical polling rates)\n- **Features NOT found:** no sorting, no price-per-metric, no CPU benchmarks, no\n  price history, no comparison view.\n- **Bottom line:** a pure filter+webhook monitor sold as infrastructure, not a\n  dashboard. This is a useful signal: even a\n  benchmark-comparison-focused writer treated the auction's constantly-rotating,\n  heterogeneous CPU inventory as too much of a moving target for a static join —\n  which is exactly the kind of pipeline work this project is committing to\n  automate.\n- **ServerHunter (serverhunter.com)** and **serverlist.dev:** multi-provider\n  (79,000+ servers across ~930 hosting companies) price/availability comparison\n  engines. Long-running (ServerHunter since 2013/2018), 24-hour refresh, stock\n  alerts every 15 minutes. Not Hetzner-auction-specific and no evidence of CPU\n  benchmark integration — they compare list-price hosting plans generally, not\n  the Dutch-auction mechanic specifically.\n- **Geekbench Browser (browser.geekbench.com) / VPSBenchmarks / BareMetalBench:**\n  these are where actual Geekbench/YABS benchmark *runs* for specific\n  Hetzner-auction-purchased machines end up — individual buyers post results after\n  the fact (e.g. \"Hetzner Server Auction i5-12500,\" \"Hetzner - Auction Server Yab\n  October 2024\"). This is real Geekbench data that exists in the wild tied to\n  Hetzner auction hardware, but it is **disconnected, manual, and after-the-fact**:\n  nobody has joined this data back onto the *live* auction feed for filtering or\n  sorting. It's a corpus that a future benchmark-matching pipeline could\n  potentially mine, not a competing product.\n- **API client libraries** (`hrobot-rs`, `aszlig/hetzner`, `Radiergummi/hetzner-api-client`,\n  `nl2go/hetzner-robot-api-mock`): general-purpose Hetzner Robot API clients in\n  Rust/Python/Node used to *build* tools like the above. Not end-user products\n  themselves; noted only because they surfaced heavily in searches for\n  \"Hetzner auction JSON parser.\"\n- **Official Hetzner Server Auction FAQ** (docs.hetzner.com): confirms the native\n  UI supports basic filtering (price, RAM, drive count, free-text like \"Epyc\" /\n  \"Xeon\" / \"DDR4\") but documents no sorting beyond that, no API, no refresh-rate\n  disclosure, and no performance/benchmark data of any kind — the floor every\n  third-party tool is improving on.\n\n---\n\n## Feature landscape: table-stakes vs. differentiating vs. gaps\n\n### Table stakes (present in nearly every tool surveyed)\n- Filter by **price**, **RAM**, **disk type/size**, **CPU model or core count**,\n  and **location/datacenter** — every single tool above implements this core set.\n- Some form of **alerting/notification** (email, Discord, Slack, Telegram,\n  webhook, Pushover, etc.) is present in 7 of the 11 direct tools — it's more\n  common than not, especially among the bot-style tools.\n- Polling cadence in the **5–15 minute** range is the norm across every tool that\n  documents it (Server Radar: 5 min; gethetzner.com: 5 min; Apify actor default:\n  10 min; hetzner-cli hosted cache: 15 min) — this roughly tracks how often\n  Hetzner's own Dutch-auction prices step down.\n- ECC and NVMe/SSD/HDD as explicit boolean/enum filters are near-universal once a\n  tool has any disk/RAM filtering at all.\n\n### Common, but not universal\n- **Price-per-metric** (€/GB RAM, €/TB storage) — present as an aggregate stat in\n  Server Radar's `/statistics` page, and as a per-listing sort key in hzfind\n  (GB/€ for RAM and storage), but most of the notification-bot-style tools skip it\n  entirely.\n- **Price history / trend tracking** — Server Radar (3 months) and\n  Server Auction Tracker (SQLite, claimed) have it; most others (Auction Browser+,\n  hzfind, all the bots) do not.\n- **Sorting** beyond simple price ascending — well-developed in hetzner-cli\n  (11 sort keys) and hzfind (3 value-based sorts), largely absent from the\n  notification bots, which only match/alert rather than rank.\n- **Shareable/saved filter configurations** — Server Auction Tracker's shareable\n  URLs and the Discord/Apify bots' persisted per-user filters are the only\n  examples; most web dashboards don't appear to persist a \"saved search\" concept\n  beyond an alert rule.\n- **Genuine API access** — only the Apify actor (paid, general-purpose) and\n  hetzner-cli / hrobot-rs (open-source client libraries, not hosted APIs) qualify.\n  Neither of the two leading dashboards (Server Radar, Auction Browser+) exposes a\n  documented public API for third parties to build on.\n\n### Rare / differentiating\n- **CPU benchmark score joined onto listings** — found in only **3 of 11** direct\n  tools (Auction Browser+, hzfind, Server Auction Tracker), and **all three use\n  PassMark exclusively**; none use Geekbench, SPEC, or any multi-source benchmark.\n  Notably, the single most popular and actively maintained tool in the entire\n  space (Server Radar, 366 stars, updated the day of this research) has **no**\n  benchmark integration at all — the market leader on every other axis (history,\n  alerts, polish, maintenance) skips the one thing this project is centered on.\n- **Blended \"value score\"** combining CPU + RAM + storage + network into one\n  number — only Auction Browser+ (public methodology: PassMark + ECC bonus +\n  storage-type weighting + bandwidth/TDP) and Server Auction Tracker (claimed:\n  weighted 0.25/0.20/0.15/... blend, 0-100 scale) attempt this; hzfind deliberately\n  keeps CPU/RAM/storage value-per-euro as three separate numbers rather than\n  blending them.\n- **Comparison/side-by-side views** — only Auction Browser+ mentions this.\n- **Cluster/fleet capacity simulation** — unique to Server Auction Tracker\n  (claimed), no other tool attempts it.\n- **Auto-buy / sniping** — only Server Auction Tracker claims this (Hetzner Robot\n  API order automation with safety gates), and it's the least-verified tool in the\n  survey (0 GitHub stars, UI not independently renderable). No other tool\n  attempts automated purchasing; everything else stops at \"notify a human.\"\n- **Browser extension** — none found. Every tool in this space is either a\n  standalone web dashboard, a CLI/TUI, or a chat bot. A Chrome/Firefox extension\n  that overlays benchmark scores directly on Hetzner's own auction page appears to\n  be unexplored territory.\n\n### Where the CPU-benchmark angle specifically stands\nThree small/medium tools (Auction Browser+, hzfind, Server Auction Tracker) have\nalready proven the *core idea* — joining PassMark scores onto live auction\nlistings and sorting by value-per-euro is technically straightforward and has\nbeen done, more than once, independently. So the raw concept is **not a blue-ocean\ngap**. But every existing implementation has real limitations this project can\ntarget:\n\n1. **Single-benchmark-source, unverified coverage.** All three use PassMark only;\n   the one that discloses coverage (Server Auction Tracker) covers \"~90 processor\n   models\" — likely incomplete given how many distinct refurb CPU SKUs rotate\n   through the auction. None cross-check against Geekbench, and the real\n   Geekbench/YABS data that does exist for Hetzner auction hardware\n   (browser.geekbench.com, VPSBenchmarks, BareMetalBench) sits disconnected from\n   any of these tools — it's a corpus nobody has mined back into a live feed.\n2. **Benchmark integration and \"tool quality\" haven't coincided.** The tool with\n   the best benchmark implementation (Auction Browser+) has no price history and\n   modest traffic; the tool with the best history/alerts/polish (Server Radar) has\n   no benchmark at all. Nobody has combined \"Server-Radar-grade maintenance and\n   data depth\" with \"PassMark-grade value scoring.\"\n3. **No performance-normalized history or alerting.** Every history feature found\n   tracks raw €, not €-per-benchmark-point over time; every alert feature found\n   thresholds on raw price/spec, not on a value score. \"Alert me when €/PassMark\n   drops below X\" does not appear to exist anywhere in this survey.\n4. **No workload-aware scoring.** Auction Browser+'s Total Score and Server\n   Auction Tracker's weighted score are each a single fixed blend; nothing lets a\n   user weight single-thread vs. multi-thread performance (or CPU vs. RAM vs.\n   storage) for their own workload.\n5. **Even benchmark-aware, non-auction tooling treats the auction as too volatile\n   to bother with** (achromatic.dev explicitly excludes it) — which is really a\n   statement that the auction's constant CPU-inventory churn makes maintaining an\n   accurate benchmark join genuinely hard, i.e. it's a real moat, not just\n   unclaimed territory. This validates `docs/notes/benchmark-priority.md`'s framing\n   that the benchmark join, done well and kept accurate, is the one piece of real\n   engineering work here — everything else (filter/sort UI, price display) is\n   solved territory that Server Radar and hetzner-cli already demonstrate how to\n   do well.\n\n**Net assessment:** CPU-benchmark-joining on Hetzner auction listings is a proven,\nreplicated idea (3 independent implementations), so it is not a novel concept —\nbut it has never been done at the data-quality/breadth level (multi-source\nbenchmarks, verified CPU coverage) or combined with the feature depth (price\nhistory, alerting, maintenance cadence) that the market leader in every other\ndimension (Server Radar) already has. The gap is not \"benchmark scores don't\nexist elsewhere,\" it's \"nobody has paired good benchmark data with a\nwell-maintained, full-featured dashboard, and nobody normalizes history/alerts by\nperformance rather than raw price.\"\n","numLines":394,"startLine":1,"totalLines":394}}}
